c: The Coming of the Lord as Judge
The Bible is clear that there will be a day of judgment (
), and the book of James provides followers of Christ with both a warning and a promise regarding that day. James announces the future coming of the Lord as Judge (
). God, who gave the law, is the Judge who has the power to save and destroy (
). Those who slander Jesus Christ and oppress his followers will be slaughtered (see
). If those who follow Christ neglect to show mercy (
), or live to satisfy evil desires (
), they, too, will be judged by the law that was intended to set them free (
The Lord’s future coming influences present realities. God already honors the faithful poor and humiliates the exploitative rich (
). Christ’s followers have already become God’s prized possession as God is restoring all things (
). James declares that we should obey the royal law of the messianic kingdom (
), of which followers of Christ have become heirs (
The coming of the Lord may not be immediate, so James exhorts Christians to endure (
) and wait patiently for Christ’s return (
). They will receive the crown of eternal life (
) and reap the harvest of righteousness sown by a life of faithfulness to God (
In view of impending judgment, James exhorts Christ’s followers to resist the devil and to humble themselves before God (
). We must grieve over sin, live with pure intentions and behavior (
), and rescue any Christian brother or sister who is headed toward death (
). Like Elijah, we must practice faith, prayer, and confession (
). Like Job, we must endure suffering, discovering in the end the scope of God’s kindness and mercy (
